0.long_answer: Treponema pallidum is a microaerophilic, gram-negative spirochete responsible for syphilis, including manifestations such as syphilitic leukoplakia. This bacterium penetrates mucous membranes or abraded skin during sexual contact and can cause various local and systemic lesions. Syphilitic leukoplakia, a white lesion in the oral cavity, is one of the clinical presentations associated with this infection.
